objective.statement: Make the synced WezTerm configuration open the Windows client directly into the devbox's native WezTerm multiplexer and stop launching the obsolete Vega/PowerShell/tmux path.
objective.measure: The source config contains the named devbox WezTerm SSHMUX domain, Windows startup selects connect devbox, Linux-side parsing completes without a Windows launcher, and the activation build succeeds.

need.statement: The active configuration still invokes powershell.exe and a six-month-old Vega/tmux wrapper even though the intended topology is Windows WezTerm GUI to the devbox's native WezTerm mux.
stakeholders: Mikael using WezTerm on a Windows client and devbox
need.baseline: The source config contains vega_tmux and powershell.exe; the reported Linux PATH cannot resolve powershell.exe.
need.consequence_of_no_action: The client keeps opening a dead Vega launcher instead of the persistent devbox WezTerm mux.
assumptions: The Windows client has the declared SSH identity and can resolve the devbox endpoint.
alternatives_considered: Keep using the obsolete Vega/tmux wrapper
Use plain SSH without WezTerm multiplexing
Use the native devbox WezTerm SSHMUX domain

purpose: Make the synced WezTerm configuration open the Windows client directly into the devbox's native WezTerm multiplexer and stop launching the obsolete Vega/PowerShell/tmux path.
consumer: Mikael using WezTerm on a Windows client with the devbox as the remote mux host.
contract: The source WezTerm configuration defines a named devbox SSH domain using WezTerm multiplexing and /home/mhugo/.local/bin/wezterm; Windows GUI startup selects connect devbox; no Vega, powershell.exe, or tmux launcher remains; the Linux-side remote mux uses its local login shell.
failure_boundary: If the devbox endpoint or client key is unavailable, WezTerm reports the connection failure; it must not fall back to the removed Vega/PowerShell/tmux path, and this change does not modify remote runtime state or credentials.

evidence.description: Failing stale-launcher absence proof, focused source assertions, direct SSH binary check, headless Linux mux parser run, and Home Manager activation build.

falsifier.claim: The managed config starts the native devbox WezTerm mux without the obsolete launcher.

executable_check.description: The source still contains a stale launcher, the required devbox fields are absent, the Linux mux parser fails, the activation build fails, or a client-side connect cannot attach.
executable_check.command: ! rg -n 'powershell\.exe|vega_tmux|vega\.ts\.hugo\.dk|tmux new' config/wezterm/wezterm.lua && rg -n 'name = "devbox"|multiplexing = "WezTerm"|remote_wezterm_path|default_gui_startup_args = \{ "connect", "devbox" \}' config/wezterm/wezterm.lua && ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 cc-se-sto-devbox-01.centralcloud.com 'test "$(command -v wezterm)" = /home/mhugo/.local/bin/wezterm'

non_goals: Change SSH keys or remote runtime state
Modify unrelated primary dotfiles checkout edits
Install a GUI library on the headless devbox
invariants: The remote multiplexer is WezTerm, not tmux or Zellij
The Windows startup path names only the devbox domain
The Linux-side config never executes a Windows-only launcher
The dotfiles primary checkout's unrelated edits remain untouched

assumptions.statement: The target WezTerm release supports ssh_domains with multiplexing=WezTerm, remote_wezterm_path, default_gui_startup_args, and named DomainName spawn actions.
assumptions.falsifier: The target client rejects one of these documented fields during config load.

assumptions.statement: The Windows client key path expands from wezterm.home_dir to the configured personal-admin key.
assumptions.falsifier: Test-Path on the Windows client returns false or connect reports an unusable identity file.

plane_constraints: Keep the change to the managed WezTerm source and its work packet; do not activate other profiles.
